briefing.opening: Good morning. I will begin the climate change expert spokesperson briefing on August 18, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Climate Disasters and Unprecedented Expansion of Impacts
sections.content: Climate-related news reported today clearly demonstrates the severity of extreme climate disasters accelerating globally. Domestically, torrential rainfall, dubbed 'water bombs,' occurred in Geoje and Tongyeong [3], and the Gyeongnam region is experiencing complex disasters becoming commonplace, suffering from extreme droughts followed by extreme downpours [14]. These abnormal climate phenomena are accompanied by warnings that 'once-in-200-year downpours' are occurring annually and unpredictable disaster-level rainfall will become more frequent [10, 58], leading to warnings of economic losses amounting to 1,000 trillion won due to drought and heavy rain [12]. Internationally, unprecedented high-temperature phenomena are being recorded in European oceans [59, 62], severe rainfall and floods are occurring across the United States, and wildfires and heatwaves are emerging as the biggest security threats in Europe [65, 67]. In particular, the world is currently experiencing a 'Super El Niño,' expected to be the strongest on record, raising concerns about a reorganization of global weather patterns [82].

sections.title: ⚠️ Climate Crisis Adaptation Efforts and Policy, Economic Challenges
sections.content: As the climate crisis intensifies, adaptation efforts to address it, along with policy and economic challenges, are emerging. In South America, the establishment of an 'Amazon Climate Adaptation Health System' is being discussed to respond to the increase in infectious diseases due to the climate crisis [1], while domestically, the 'climate insurance' market is expanding as the climate crisis deepens, and the government plans to further expand it [2, 6]. However, criticism has also been raised that the carbon reduction targets in the revised plan are uncertain and that the state is neglecting its responsibility to respond to the climate crisis [25]. The possibility of the stock market facing climate change-related issues has been raised [66], and the recognition that climate change should be included in future crop market risks is spreading [70], indicating severe impacts across the economy. Furthermore, discussions are actively underway regarding methods to address climate change denial [60, 74] and the role of the media in encouraging citizen change by reporting on the causes of the climate crisis [76].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Practices and Expansion of Citizen Participation
sections.content: Efforts for carbon neutrality practices and citizen participation are actively continuing across various regions in South Korea to respond to the climate crisis. Dobong-gu plans to establish a comprehensive plan for creating a carbon-neutral city and address climate inequality [15, 20, 26], while Gimhae City has shown exemplary cases, such as donating 16.67 million won in carbon neutrality point incentives [16, 23, 36, 37]. Suwon Climate Change Experience Education Center and Suwon FC are carrying out a 'Climate Crisis Escape Operation' [7, 11], and Sacheon City is striving to raise public awareness through education and campaigns, including conducting carbon neutrality practice education for children and parents [17]. Resident-participatory activities such as Gwangmyeong City's 'Climate Militia' and Guro-gu's 'G-Guro Guardians' are gaining attention [21], and Chungju City is also continuously recruiting participants for its carbon neutrality point energy sector, providing incentives for energy reduction [22, 34].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Exploring Regional Co-prosperity Models
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is accelerating nationwide, and efforts to build models that foster co-prosperity with local communities are notable. Siheung City achieved the feat of saving approximately 20 million won annually by installing customized renewable energy facilities in three public facilities [41, 42, 45, 46, 48, 50]. Yesan County achieved the remarkable accomplishment of being selected for new and renewable energy public projects for 10 consecutive years, earning an 'excellent' rating in the top 10% nationwide [43, 44, 47]. In particular, Haenam County, Jeollanam-do, is actively exploring renewable energy models that promote co-prosperity with local communities, including establishing 'Haenam-type Renewable Energy Management Plans' related to large-scale solar power development and setting standards for farmland preservation and profit sharing [49, 52, 53, 55, 56]. Internationally, the movement towards renewable energy transition is also active, with Son La Province in Vietnam, for example, expanding the application of renewable energy technologies [51].

briefing.closing: Through today's briefing, we have been able to confirm the reality of unprecedented climate disasters and the various domestic and international efforts to combat them. Responding to the climate crisis is an urgent task that can no longer be postponed, requiring active participation and continuous innovation from everyone. This concludes today's climate briefing.
